sections.h2: Where is Springville, Utah, and what is it known for?
sections.html:
Springville is a Utah County city on the west side of the Wasatch Range, about 3 miles east of the average shoreline of Utah Lake. Wikipedia lists it at 14.4 square miles and an elevation of 4,554 feet, and it sits almost entirely east of Interstate 15.

The city's nickname is Art City. The Springville Museum of Art, founded around 1937, is described as Utah's oldest museum for visual fine arts, and sculptor Cyrus Dallin was born here.

Springville is in Utah County, so your assessor, treasurer and recorder are the county offices in Provo, and Nebo School District serves the city.

sections.h2: How did Springville begin, and how did it change?
sections.html:
Aaron Johnson led eight pioneer families to the site on September 18, 1850, and the settlement was first called Hobble Creek. It was later renamed for the nearby springs and for Fort Springville, and incorporation followed in 1853.

The Utah History Encyclopedia describes an economy that moved from livestock grazing and subsistence farming to sugar beets and fruit grown for national canning companies. In 1922, L.F. Rains formed Columbia Steel Corporation at Ironton to produce pig iron, and the town also hosted cast-iron pipe production and creosoting.

The same source says interstate construction in the 1960s moved traffic out of town and that Springville became a bedroom community. Wikipedia expects future commercial, office, retail and industrial building along the I-15 corridor.

sections.h2: What do the official numbers say about Springville housing?
sections.html:
Springville is a younger, family-oriented city where about seven in ten homes are owner-occupied. These are Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

Population (2020 Census)35,268

Owner-occupied housing rate71.7%

Persons per household3.25

The 2020 count is a 19.7% increase over 2010, and the median age was 28.5.

Food production and manufacturing remain the best-documented employers. The Utah History Encyclopedia names Stouffer Foods with more than 500 employees and Valtek with more than 400 as current major employers.

  • Nebo School District operates Springville High School, Springville Junior High, Spring Canyon Middle School and several elementary schools.
  • The Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind has its Elizabeth DeLong School campus in Springville, built at a cost of $13 million.
  • Charter schools include Reagan Academy and Merit Academy.

Wikipedia describes the city as a bedroom community for people who work in the Provo-Orem and Salt Lake City areas and expects commercial, office and industrial growth along the I-15 corridor.

sections.h2: Can I rent out part of a Springville house?
sections.html:
Yes, but the city sets specific ownership and occupancy conditions. Springville's ADU FAQ says accessory dwelling units are allowed only in single-family residential zones, and duplexes, twin homes and apartments cannot have one.

  • The owner must hold at least 50% of the property.
  • Either the main house or the ADU must be owner-occupied, and both cannot be rentals.
  • A building permit is required for interior conversions and for detached ADUs.
  • Short-term rentals of under 30 days need a city business license, and the host must live in the main dwelling and be present.

The city says renting the top and bottom of a house to separate tenants depends on the zone and on whether the second unit was created legally with a permit or is a legal nonconforming use. If your basement apartment was never permitted, tell the buyer before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: What permits and inspections matter in Springville?
sections.html:
A building permit is required before you enlarge, repair, alter, add to or demolish a structure or install equipment in it. The city building division lists state guidelines for work that is exempt.

Inspections must be provided within three business days of a request, and the city does not offer same-day inspections. Requests submitted after 5:00 p.m. Friday through Sunday night count as received Monday, and the building office is at 801-489-2704.

If you remodeled without a permit, a buyer's inspector or lender may ask about it. Pull the permit history from the city before you list.

sections.h2: How are utilities handled in Springville?
sections.html:
The city runs its own power department, water and public works. The Springville Power Department's page names the Whitehead Power Plant, lists a Customer Generation program that covers solar systems, and gives (801) 489-2750 for outages and billing questions.

The city's culinary water page links an annual water quality report, and its home page posts recycling pickup on an alternating two-week schedule. A buyer moving in will need to set up city utility accounts, so mention that in your closing checklist.

sections.h2: What events and landmarks define Springville?
sections.html:
Springville's calendar follows its arts identity. Wikipedia lists Art City Days in early June, the Springville World Folkfest in July and the Indian Festival of Utah in May.

The city's own events page lists City Council meetings on November 3 and 17 and Planning Commission meetings on November 10 and 24, 2026, all at 7 p.m. Planning Commission agendas are where zoning changes near your street first appear.

sections.h2: Do earthquakes and radon matter when selling in Springville?
sections.html:
They can come up during a buyer's inspection. The Wasatch Fault has ten segments, five of them active, including the Provo segment, and Wikipedia reports a 57% estimated chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake in the next 50 years.

Utah's radon program says one in three Utah homes has elevated radon, using 4 picocuries per liter as its action level. A short test before listing tells you whether the number is a surprise.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work in Springville?
sections.html:
Utah County bills Springville property, and the last day to pay without a penalty is November 30. The county Auditor mails a valuation notice each year, and a separate tax notice is mailed between the middle and end of October.

If you disagree with the value, file with the Board of Equalization by the later of September 15 or 45 days after the notice is mailed. Missing that deadline makes the listed value final for the year. Primary residences get a 45% exemption.

The Treasurer's office is at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1200, Provo, and the phone is 801-851-8255. Ask for a payoff figure, since prior-year delinquencies are not included in the bill. The Recorder, at Suite 1300 and 801-851-8179, files your deed.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Springville?
sections.html:
A cash buyer pays without a mortgage, so the sale does not wait on an appraisal or loan approval. You describe the house, review the written offer and pick a closing date.

The closing takes place at a title or escrow company, and the deed is recorded in Provo. Taxes are prorated, and any unpermitted ADU or addition should be disclosed up front.

sections.h2: What do Springville sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
• Basement apartments without a permit or a clear owner-occupancy history.
  • Short-term rental use where the host did not live in the main dwelling.
  • Remodel work done without a building permit.
  • Belongings left behind in an inherited house.

faqs.a: Yes. Utah County handles valuation, tax billing and deed recording, and Nebo School District serves the city.

faqs.q: When are Springville property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay without a penalty. Utah County mails the tax notice between mid and late October.

faqs.q: Can I have a basement apartment in Springville?
faqs.a: Only as a permitted ADU in a single-family zone. The owner must own at least 50% and live in either the main house or the ADU, and a building permit is required.

faqs.q: How many people live in Springville?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 35,268 people, up 19.7% from 29,466 in 2010.

faqs.q: Do I need a license for a short-term rental in Springville?
faqs.a: Yes. Rentals under 30 days need a city business license, and the host must live in the main dwelling and be present.
